newsitem.title: MEXICO: Gunmen shoot up Mexico newspaper building.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen shoot up Mexico newspaper building.

text.p: A northern Mexican newspaper appealed to President Ernesto Zedillo on Thursday to investigate a gun attack on its headquarters after it printed stories about a corrupt police chief.

Norte de Ciudad Juarez, a daily based in the border town of Ciudad Juarez, just across from El Paso, Texas, took out an advertisement on Thursday in a Mexico City paper asking Zedillo to step in and defend press freedom.

Vicente Jaime, the director-general of Norte de Ciudad Juarez, told Reuters that one or more gunmen fired a burst of shots at the newspaper building in the early hours of Wednesday as that day's edition was being printed.
Bullets caused some damage to the office but employees inside escaped injury, Jaime said.

In its paid ad, Norte said it had run a series of stories exposing a "secret municipal police force" run by a policeman accused of corruption and abuses, forcing him to resign on Tuesday. Hours later, the gun attack happened.
"We can't say that these events are related ... but we believe that ... there should be an exhaustive impartial investigation," the newspaper said.
Asked if he believed thugs were attempting to intimidate the newspaper, Jaime said: "We have a lot of indications that this is the intention, but the authorities must investigate."
Juarez is home to one of Mexico's biggest drug cartels which smuggles tons of cocaine and large quantities of heroin and other drugs across the border every year.
Reforma newspaper said two other publications in Juarez, Diario de Juarez and Revista Semanal, had been threatened by drugs traffickers recently.
